A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Draft-based Approximate Inference with SpecKV and SpecPC. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original RULER, LongBench, and MileBench evaluations, latency and memory measurements, attention-correlation experiments, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds accuracy and efficiency comparisons with SpecPrefill.

M1.justification: The SpecKV and SpecPC procedures remain substantively unchanged. Window weighting and pooling already appear in v1; v2 corrects Algorithm 2's weighting index and explicitly documents position-ID reassignment, without establishing that the implemented procedure changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same RULER tasks, selected English/code LongBench tasks, and six MileBench datasets. SpecPrefill is evaluated within retained task coverage; no new domain, population, or task is demonstrated.

E2.justification: v2 adds SpecPrefill, a directly related draft-attention and lookahead method, to the central RULER, LongBench, latency, and memory comparisons (Figures 5–7 and 9; Tables 3–4 and 9–10). This substantially strengthens comparator relevance. The KV-dropping, multimodal, and larger-model comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added SpecPrefill evaluations use eight lookahead tokens and settings listed in Table 8. Figure 7 narrows the reported memory-measurement range from 128K to 64K input tokens. Table 8 also changes SpecPC's Pool entry from Max to Avg, consistent with v1's prose and pseudocode; this does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The token-importance case study, attention-correlation diagnostics, and draft-quality, lookahead-length, and sparse-prefill ablations remain unchanged (Figures 3–4, 8, and 11–13). The expanded window-size motivation in Section 5.2 supplies no additional ablation results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The attention-correlation fitting and reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The added SpecPrefill results substantially change the comparative picture. At Cmax = 1024, its LongBench aggregate scores are 43.00 for Qwen and 42.86 for Llama, versus unchanged SpecPC scores of 43.73 and 43.76; v1's best prompt-compression baselines scored 37.17 and 37.58 (Tables 3–4). Additional SpecPrefill results cover larger budgets, RULER, latency, and memory. Figure 7 removes the 128K memory results.

T1.justification: The importance-score definitions, Lemmas 1–2, Theorems 1–3, assumptions, and Appendix B proofs are retained. Equation-formatting and index-notation corrections introduce no substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: v1 claims the first use of draft models for approximate inference generally. v2 narrows the abstract and introduction's priority claim to SpecKV's KV-cache optimization, describes the framework as generalizing SpecPrefill, and calls SpecPC an iterative improvement of it. The conclusion also removes the combined first-method claim.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 adds explanations concerning task-dependent windows, avoiding static chunks that split related tokens, and position reassignment permitting inputs beyond the target's context limit. Sections 6.3 and E.1 attribute advantages over SpecPrefill to shorter lookahead. The explicit limitations and future-work discussion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents contiguous position-ID reassignment, clarifies window weights, corrects Algorithm 2's index, and supplies SpecPrefill hyperparameters, including window size 1, kernel size 13, lookahead 8, and chunk size 32. Hardware, software, decoding instructions, and code/data access disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Liu, Chen, and Zhang's Speculative Prefill and substantially revises positioning around this closely related work. Sections 1–3 and 5 acknowledge shared draft-model lookahead and attention scoring, distinguish windowing, chunking, and positional handling, and reposition SpecPC as an improvement of SpecPrefill.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites affect the abstract, contribution list, related-work discussion, and SpecPC explanation, with smaller edits to results and conclusions. The overall section order, narrative organization, and appendix structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Existing figures and tables are retained. SpecPrefill adds curves and legends to Figures 5–7 and 9, rows to Tables 3–4 and 9–10, and a column to Table 8. Figures 6–7 have axis adjustments, and Tables 3–4 and Figure 6 move with text reflow.

improvement.justification: Acknowledging and evaluating SpecPrefill substantially addresses v1's omission of closely related prior work from its novelty discussion and central comparisons. Tables 3–4 now reveal much smaller LongBench advantages over this comparator, making SpecPC's contribution more accurately assessable. These gains outweigh the limited loss of 128K memory evidence. The correction remains incomplete because Section 2 retains a conflicting broad first-use claim.
